extracted.intended_audience: academic scholars (potential authors), general readers, news organizations and donors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and editorial standards for academics who write explanatory journalism for The Conversation U.S., including who may write, how pieces are edited and distributed, and transparency/funding expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthy, informative articles by academic experts
rubrics_metrics.description: We publish trustworthy and informative articles written by academic experts for the general public and edited by our team of journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On this website ... you’ll find explanatory journalism on the events, discoveries and issues that matter today. Our articles share researchers’ expertise in policy, science, health, economics, education, history, ethics and most every subject studied in colleges and universities. Some articles offer practical advice grounded in research, while others simply provide authoritative answers to questions that sparked our curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors limited to subjects of proven expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are allowed to write only on subjects in which they have proven expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the site’s commitment to transparency and credibility; editors work with scholars but authors must have demonstrable expertise in the topic they cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of authors' relevant funding and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: They must sign a disclosure statement outlining any relevant funding or affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are required to declare relevant funding or affiliations to make potential conflicts transparent to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of organizational funders
rubrics_metrics.description: We disclose all of The Conversation U.S.’s funders on our homepage and elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site lists major funders and provides links such as the 2025 Annual Report and the most recent IRS Form 990; this disclosure supports credibility and reader trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate and collaborative editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conversation’s editorial process is deliberate and collaborative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors pay close attention to the news environment, reach out to leading scholars across academia and work with them to help them share their knowledge with the broad public; articles are edited by journalists for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and public relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors pay close attention to the news environment to identify the issues citizens are concerned about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team prioritizes topics that matter to the public now, shaping pitches and pieces to address current events, discoveries and issues of public concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory journalism across academic disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explanatory journalism that shares researchers’ expertise across a wide range of subjects (policy, science, health, economics, education, history, ethics, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content can include both practical, research-grounded advice and authoritative answers to curious questions; the goal is to translate academic knowledge for the general public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open distribution under Creative Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: Through a Creative Commons license, we distribute our articles – at no charge – to news organizations across the geographic and ideological spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy enables wide reuse and syndication; the Associated Press distributes The Conversation’s content daily to thousands of newsrooms, amplifying reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for under-resourced news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay particular attention to strengthening news organizations that are severely under-resourced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free distribution and syndication of articles is used in part to bolster local and under-resourced newsrooms by providing high-quality explanatory journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to an editorial charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Our goals are summed up in our editorial charter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial charter encapsulates the organization’s aims and presumably governs how editorial decisions, transparency and standards are applied (link provided on site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation and process for scholar pitches
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a scholar interested in writing for us, please send us a pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Conversation solicits pitches from academics and provides a mechanism for submission; editors will engage with scholars to shape and edit pieces for the public audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to transparency and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Importantly, The Conversation U.S. is committed to transparency and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overarching commitment is operationalized via author expertise requirements, disclosure statements, funder transparency, editorial oversight, and public-facing documents (annual report, IRS filings, fundraising guidelines).
